An attacker scaling up to thousands of parallel nodes faces a compounding compute penalty. Maintaining synchronized state across a dense cluster requires massive cryptographic hardware overhead. The attacker pays a direct cost in discarded compute cycles and forced bandwidth bottlenecks, rendering large-scale automated spoofing economically unviable because the sparrow of a lone honest agent travels just as fast with zero overhead.
